evals.query: Set up OpenTelemetry tracing in my Kora service and export traces over OTLP gRPC to an OpenTelemetry Collector. The service name should be order-service.
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:opentelemetry-tracing-exporter-grpc and leaves it unversioned, taking the version from platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") with koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2
Extends OpentelemetryGrpcExporterModule from io.koraframework.opentelemetry.tracing.exporter.grpc on the @KoraApp interface (@KoraApp imported from io.koraframework.common.annotation)
Sets tracing.exporter.endpoint to an OTLP gRPC URL on port 4317 with no path segment

Sets tracing.attributes."service.name" = "order-service" and explains that Kora adds no resource attribute itself: the OTLP resource is built only from OpentelemetryTracingAttributesProvider components and tracing.attributes
Includes the processor: annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" (Java) or ksp "io.koraframework:symbol-processors" (Kotlin)
Does not add io.opentelemetry:* dependencies by hand, since the OpenTelemetry API and SDK arrive transitively
anti_behavior: Uses the ru.tinkoff.kora group, kora-parent, or a Kora 1.x package name
Writes tracing.enabled = true as if tracing were off by default

evals.query: In my Kotlin Kora service I want to send traces to Jaeger over OTLP HTTP instead of gRPC.
expected_behavior: Uses io.koraframework:opentelemetry-tracing-exporter-http and extends OpentelemetryHttpExporterModule from io.koraframework.opentelemetry.tracing.exporter.http
Sets tracing.exporter.endpoint to the OTLP HTTP signal path, http://jaeger:4318/v1/traces, not a bare host:port
Replaces the gRPC module rather than extending both exporter modules at once
Mentions COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED (or equivalent) so Jaeger accepts OTLP
Keeps the config keys unchanged when switching exporters, since both exporter config interfaces declare the same keys
anti_behavior: Invents a tracing.exporter.protocol key to choose HTTP over gRPC
Adds both OpentelemetryGrpcExporterModule and OpentelemetryHttpExporterModule to the same @KoraApp

evals.query: Configure the Kora Zipkin exporter to send spans to http://zipkin:9411/api/v2/spans.
expected_behavior: States that Kora 2.0 ships only OTLP exporters -- opentelemetry-tracing-exporter-grpc and opentelemetry-tracing-exporter-http -- and has no Zipkin exporter module
Explains that /api/v2/spans is the Zipkin JSON ingest and cannot receive OTLP, so pointing a Kora exporter at it does not work
Recommends exporting OTLP to an OpenTelemetry Collector and configuring the Collector's zipkin exporter to forward to Zipkin
Reframes Zipkin as an OTLP-compatible backend behind a Collector, not as a supported Kora exporter
anti_behavior: Sets tracing.exporter.endpoint = "http://zipkin:9411/api/v2/spans" with either Kora exporter module
Presents Zipkin or Jaeger as a first-class Kora exporter choice alongside OTLP
Suggests compression = "none" as the fix for Zipkin

evals.query: My Kora service traces normal requests fine, but the liveness, readiness and /metrics calls on port 8085 never produce any spans. What is broken?
expected_behavior: Identifies that nothing is broken: SystemHttpServerConfig.SystemHttpServerTelemetryConfig.SystemHttpServerTracingConfig overrides enabled() to false, so the system server is untraced by design
Notes this is the one documented exception to TracingConfig.enabled() defaulting to true
Gives httpServer.system.telemetry.tracing.enabled = true as the way to opt in if probe spans are genuinely wanted
Warns that tracing probe traffic adds high-volume low-value spans
anti_behavior: Claims tracing defaults to false and tells the user to enable it globally
Blames the exporter endpoint, the sampler, or the collector
Suggests a config key under httpServer.system that does not exist

evals.query: Do I have to turn tracing on in Kora 2.0 the same way I have to turn metrics on?
expected_behavior: States that TracingConfig.enabled() and OpentelemetryTracingConfig.enabled() default to true, unlike the per-component LoggingConfig.enabled() and MetricsConfig.enabled() (telemetry.logging/metrics.enabled), which default to false
Explains that you therefore only ever write tracing.enabled = false, and that writing true changes nothing
Names httpServer.system as the single place where tracing is overridden to false
Points out that with tracing on but tracing.exporter.endpoint unset, spans are created and sampled but silently never exported
Explains that tracing.enabled = false swaps in TracerProvider.noop() and makes the exporter SpanExporter/SpanProcessor no-ops
anti_behavior: Tells the user to add tracing.enabled = true or <component>.telemetry.tracing.enabled = true to make tracing work
Treats tracing, metrics and logging as having the same default

evals.query: Add a span around my processOrder business method in a Java Kora service so it records the order id, reports errors, and stays inside the incoming request trace.
expected_behavior: Injects io.koraframework.opentelemetry.tracing.KoraTracer through the constructor of a @Component
Wraps the work in tracer.traceParent("order.process", span -> { ... }) so the span nests under the current one
Sets business attributes on the Span handed to the callback, e.g. span.setAttribute("order.id", order.id())
Explains that KoraTracer already sets StatusCode.OK, records the exception with StatusCode.ERROR, and ends the span, so no try/finally is needed
Uses constructor injection only -- Kora has no field injection
anti_behavior: Reads a Kora Context via Context.current() or calls OpentelemetryContext.get(ctx) / .set(ctx, ...) / .add(span)
Wraps the span in try (var scope = span.makeCurrent())
Hand-rolls the full span lifecycle when KoraTracer covers it

evals.query: Same thing in Kotlin: put a span around processOrder in my Kora service and tag it with the order id.
expected_behavior: Injects KoraTracer into a @Component constructor

Calls traceParent with an explicit SAM constructor, KoraTracer.TraceCallable<Order, RuntimeException> { span -> ... }, because the TraceCallable/TraceRunnable overload pair does not resolve from a bare Kotlin lambda
Uses KoraTracer.TraceRunnable<RuntimeException> { ... } for the no-result variant
Sets attributes on the Span parameter of the callback
anti_behavior: Passes a bare Kotlin lambda to traceParent and presents it as compiling
Uses a suspend function or withContext for the span, since Kora 2.0 has no suspend contracts
References Context.Kotlin.asCoroutineContext

evals.query: I am porting this Kora code and it no longer compiles: var ctx = Context.current(); var otctx = OpentelemetryContext.get(ctx); ... OpentelemetryContext.set(ctx, otctx.add(span)); and in finally OpentelemetryContext.set(ctx, otctx). How do I write it for Kora 2.0?
expected_behavior: States that Kora's own Context type was removed from the whole framework in 2.0 -- there is no Context.current(), no fork(), and none of get/set/add on OpentelemetryContext

Distinguishes the two remaining types clearly: io.opentelemetry.context.Context is the OpenTelemetry context, while io.koraframework.common.telemetry.OpentelemetryContext implements it and exists to hold ScopedValue<Context> VALUE
Replaces the whole block with KoraTracer.traceParent(...), or with ScopedValue.where(OpentelemetryContext.VALUE, Context.current().with(span)).call(...) when the SpanBuilder is needed
Explains that the ScopedValue binding unwinds by itself, so the finally-restore of the previous context disappears entirely (span.end() still belongs in finally)
Notes that Context.current() and Span.current() work anywhere because Kora registers OpentelemetryContextStorageProvider as the OpenTelemetry ContextStorage
anti_behavior: Keeps any Kora Context call and claims it still exists
Rewrites OpentelemetryContext.set(...) into an equivalent imperative setter
Imports OpentelemetryContext from io.koraframework.opentelemetry.common (it lives in io.koraframework.common.telemetry)

evals.query: Show me how to make my manual span the current span in Kora so downstream JDBC and HTTP client calls nest under it.
expected_behavior: Warns that span.makeCurrent() and Context.makeCurrent() throw IllegalStateException, because Kora's ContextStorage.attach(...) cannot attach to a ScopedValue
Uses ScopedValue.where(OpentelemetryContext.VALUE, Context.current().with(span)).call(...) / .run(...), or simply KoraTracer, to bind the span for a lexical scope
Confirms that once bound, framework integrations pick it up through Context.current() with no extra wiring
Points out there is nothing to close or restore -- the binding unwinds when the scope returns
anti_behavior: Produces a try (Scope scope = span.makeCurrent()) block
Suggests a ThreadLocal or an MDC entry as the propagation mechanism

evals.query: Review my Kora tracing config: tracing { exporter { endpoint = "http://otel:4317", protocol = "grpc", retry { maxAttempts = 3 } }, sampler { probability = 0.1 } }
expected_behavior: Flags protocol as non-existent: the wire protocol comes from the exporter artifact and module, not from config
Flags retry as the wrong key -- the nested section is retryPolicy, with maxAttempts / initialBackoff / maxBackoff / backoffMultiplier
Flags tracing.sampler as non-existent and directs sampling to an opentelemetryTracingSampler() override on the @KoraApp interface
Warns that unknown HOCON keys are ignored without a warning, so the retry and sampler blocks silently do nothing
Confirms endpoint and its 4317 value are correct for the gRPC exporter
anti_behavior: Accepts protocol, retry or sampler as valid keys
Invents tracing.exporter.headers or tracing.exporter.enabled

evals.query: I only want to sample about 10 percent of traces in production. How do I configure the sampler in Kora?
expected_behavior: Explains that sampling is a graph component, not configuration, and there is no tracing.sampler key
Overrides opentelemetryTracingSampler() on the @KoraApp interface, replacing the @DefaultComponent Sampler.parentBased(Sampler.alwaysOn())
Marks the override with @Override in Java (or the override keyword in Kotlin) and notes the processor keys on it to drop the module's declaration
Returns Sampler.parentBased(Sampler.traceIdRatioBased(0.1)) from io.opentelemetry.sdk.trace.samplers, keeping parentBased so children honour the caller's decision
Optionally drives the ratio from an injected @ConfigSource interface, since the override is an ordinary component method
anti_behavior: Adds tracing.sampler.probability, tracing.sampler.type or tracing.exporter.sampler to the config
Returns a bare traceIdRatioBased without parentBased and claims traces stay whole

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 app starts clean, I never touched tracing.enabled, and there is not a single span in the collector. Nothing in the logs. Where do I look?
expected_behavior: Checks tracing.exporter.endpoint first: it is nullable with no default, and when null both spanExporter and spanProcessor fall back to composite() no-ops with no log line and no startup failure
Points at environment substitution as the usual reason the endpoint resolves empty
Checks that the endpoint shape matches the module -- gRPC on 4317 with no path, HTTP on 4318/v1/traces
Checks whether the traffic hits httpServer.system, whose tracing is off by default
Notes that the HTTP server builds no span for an unrouted request, since pathTemplate() is null on a 404
Suggests raising io.koraframework.opentelemetry / io.opentelemetry.exporter log levels
anti_behavior: Tells the user to set tracing.enabled = true
Claims a missing endpoint fails at startup or logs a warning

evals.query: I hand some work to an ExecutorService inside a Kora request handler and the spans created there start their own trace. How do I carry the trace across?
expected_behavior: Captures io.opentelemetry.context.Context.current() on the originating thread, before submitting
Wraps the task with context.wrap(runnable) / wrap(callable) / wrapSupplier(...), which OpentelemetryContext implements on top of ScopedValue.where(...)
Explains that a ScopedValue binding is not inherited by an unrelated thread, so the context must travel with the task
Notes that a span outliving the submitting scope must be started before the hop and ended inside the task or its completion callback
Mentions that synchronous contracts on virtual threads usually make the hop unnecessary in the first place
anti_behavior: Uses a removed Kora Context.fork()
Calls Context.current() inside the task body and expects the caller's context
Reaches for CompletionStage, Mono/Flux or suspend as a Kora contract

evals.query: I want the trace id in my Kora log lines but I do not have a collector to export to yet. Is that possible?
expected_behavior: Says yes: add io.koraframework:opentelemetry-tracing and extend OpentelemetryTracingModule without any exporter module
Explains that SpanProcessor is a @Nullable dependency, so with no exporter it resolves to SpanProcessor.composite() -- real spans are created and sampled, nothing is exported
Notes that correlation needs no configuration: KoraAsyncAppender captures Span.current().getSpanContext() and ConsoleTextRecordEncoder prints traceId= when that span context is valid
Reads the current trace id in code with Span.current().getSpanContext().getTraceId(), guarded by isValid()
anti_behavior: Claims an exporter artifact is mandatory to get trace ids
Uses a removed OpentelemetryContext.getTraceId() / getSpan() accessor
Adds an MDC key by hand to carry the trace id

evals.query: I want every exported span of my Kora 2.0 Java service to carry service.instance.id from the HOSTNAME environment variable and the build version from the jar manifest, computed at startup. service.name is already in tracing.attributes.
expected_behavior: Implements io.koraframework.opentelemetry.tracing.OpentelemetryTracingAttributesProvider in a @Component class returning Map<String, String> from attributes()

Explains that OpentelemetryTracingModule collects every provider through All<OpentelemetryTracingAttributesProvider> and puts their attributes on the OpenTelemetry Resource, so they apply to every span
States that tracing.attributes is applied after the providers and wins on a key conflict, so service.name stays in config
Notes that attributes() is called once while the graph builds the Resource
Uses OpenTelemetry resource semantic-convention keys (service.instance.id, service.version) and a fallback such as "unknown" for missing values
anti_behavior: Adds the values as per-component telemetry.tracing.attributes or sets them on each span by hand
Replaces the @DefaultComponent Resource with a hand-built one when a provider suffices
Claims the provider overrides tracing.attributes

evals.query: My OpentelemetryTracingAttributesProvider returns service.name = order-service-canary, but traces still show order-service. tracing.attributes has "service.name" = "order-service". Is the provider not registered?
expected_behavior: Explains that the provider is registered: opentelemetryTracingResource puts every provider's attributes first and tracing.attributes last, so the config value wins on the service.name key
Fixes it by removing service.name from tracing.attributes (or computing it in config with an environment substitution) rather than expecting the provider to override config
anti_behavior: Claims providers are applied after config
Suggests a tracing.resource or tracing.attributesProvider config key
